subject: inference under spde model with known variance and scale parameters

messages.author: 40cb5026d0e9f97c
messages.subject: inference under spde model with known variance and scale parameters
parts:
I would like to do inference with a formula along the line of 
myformula =(z ~ 1 + f(spatial, model=spde) + y)
where the spatial and scale parameters for the random field are known and fixed to  some values.

How would I do that?
Thx

G.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inference under spde model with known variance and scale parameters
parts:
[Initial reply didn't go to the list. /FL]
Note: This reply deals only with the "spde with fixed parameters" bit,
and assumes general knowledge of how to do inference with inla.

On 7 November 2012 15:03, gg <gilles.b...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I would like to do inference with a formula along the line of
> myformula =(z ~ 1 + f(spatial, model=spde) + y)
> where the spatial and scale parameters for the random field are known and
> fixed to some values.
>
> How would I do that?

Hi,

first you need to figure out what tau and kappa should be in the SPDE
model. How that can be done depends on your definition of "range".
With the definitions used in the SPDE/GMRF paper,
kappa = sqrt(8*\nu)/range,
where nu=alpha-dim/2, so nu=1 when alpha=2 and dim=2.
For alpha=2 and dim=2, the field variance is given by
\sigma^2 = 1/( 4\pi \kappa^2 \tau^2)
so that
\tau = 1/( 4\pi \kappa^2 \sigma^2)^0.5

Then, construct the spde model object like this:

spde=inla.spde2.matern(mesh,B.tau=matrix(log(tau),1,1),B.kappa=matrix(log(kappa),1,1))

this gives an spde model with no parameters, and the given values for
tau and kappa, by specifying them as offsets (in log scale), and no
basis functions for which to apply any "theta".

/Finn



> Thx
>
> G.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inference under spde model with known variance and scale parameters
parts:
On 08/11/13 13:46, Alex wrote:
> I am trying to do the same where log(tau) (and/or log(kappa)) is a known
> vector on the mesh but it estimates the hyperpars.
> How would I need to specify the Bs in that case?

Simply expand the B-matrices into column matrices:

spde=inla.spde2.matern(mesh,
B.tau=matrix(log(tau), mesh$n, 1),
B.kappa=matrix(log(kappa), mesh$n, 1))

If tau and kappa are vectors of length mesh$m that should give you what
you ask for.

Finn
